Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games.
  • One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does.
  • "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion.

One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

Humphries indicates this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6, Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained.

Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's vital is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world.".

It has been revealed that this is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts. And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does.

Sources indicate that rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mark says he finished his omelet and headed back to Latest York.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One day in August 2019, Mark Epstein was having breakfast at a Virginia hotel when he looked at the TV and saw CNN reporting that his older brother, Jeffrey Epstein, had died by suicide in a Manhattan federal prison. As jarring as the news was, he had no reason to doubt it.

Recent findings suggest that “I knew he wouldn’t want to live the rest of his life in jail,” Mark told Vanity Fair this week. “He had no children to worry about. Our parents were gone. He knew he didn’t have to worry about me.”.

Mark says he finished his omelet and headed back to Latest York. Then, like so many other Americans, he started to become skeptical of the official narrative.

Over the last seven years, the endless conspiracy theories surrounding Jeffrey Epstein’s death have largely been relegated to the backwaters of YouTube and Reddit, while local and federal authorities have stuck to the suicide story. But this week there was a breakthrough. On Monday, Michael Freeman, a leading forensic scientist who testified for the prosecution in the trial of Derek Chauvin for the murder of George Floyd, issued the most legitimate challenge to date to the prevailing consensus.

Freeman presented his findings at a historic London legal society, saying, “The pattern and distribution and multitude of injuries are not explained by a suicidal hanging.” In a Upcoming York Times story published the same day as the presentation, Freeman told the paper that he had no view on who might have killed Jeffrey: “All I’m interested in is, how did this get so sideways?” Along with several global news organizations, including CBS and the BBC, the Times covered the development with a straight face even as it noted that Freeman’s efforts to publish his findings in a peer-reviewed journal had thus far been rejected.

The relationship between Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein has loomed large over the president’s second term.

In his thick Brooklyn accent, Mark Epstein, who has long been trying to prove that his brother was murdered while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges, excitedly recounted this milestone over the phone the day after Freeman’s presentation, which he attended.

Sources indicate that “This crosses all party lines,” Mark mentioned. “Most people believe he didn’t commit suicide. So it’s a mystery. People want an answer to that. I think now they have the answer.”.

Mark emphasized that the story of the recent findings was not about him but rather about his brother’s death and Freeman’s work. It was Freeman who reached out to him, Mark said, based on what the scientist independently thought was shoddy work on Jeffrey’s autopsy, and Mark agreed to turn over all the records, reports, and photographs he had as next of kin.

“I want to make it really clear,” he said. “I didn’t pay for this. He’s never asked me for anything other than the information, which I gave him willingly. And he’s been studying this. As a matter of fact, the night before last was the first time I ever met him face-to-face.”.

Still, Mark has made his suspicions both his calling card and his personal mission in recent years. After working in real estate investing and serving as the chair of Cooper Union’s board of trustees, he had his own business dealings come under some scrutiny as Jeffrey’s life and crimes dominated political and cultural discourse beginning in the late 2010s—Jeffrey allegedly housed models and employees in an Upper East Side building that was predominantly owned by his brother’s real estate holding company. In the years since his brother’s death, Mark has remarked that Jeffrey “definitely had dirt” on Donald Trump, and he became a minor fixation amid the Epstein files rollout on account of emails containing banter between him and his brother. (Trump has denied any prior knowledge of Jeffrey’s crimes and said that the release of the Epstein files “totally exonerated” him.) Mark has dismissed a suicide note purportedly written by Jeffrey as a fabrication.

Jeffrey’s death certificate initially said “pending further study” in regard to the cause of death, rather than ruling it a homicide or suicide, but the chief medical examiner ruled it a suicide days later. “All the pathologists I’ve spoken to,” says Mark, “they said, [if] an initial death certificate says ‘pending further study,’ you don’t get an answer usually for weeks or more because something’s being studied.” Mark hired the celebrity forensic pathologist Michael Baden to observe and evaluate the autopsy, and Baden previously stated that “the evidence points to homicide.” Federal officials’ handling of the matter in the years to come only amplified Mark’s concern.

“You know a suicide when you see one,” FBI director Kash Patel stated last year while he was under fire for not producing any proof of the Epstein conspiracies he had been touting during his time as a mere conservative podcast personality, “and that’s what that was.”.

“I actually laughed out loud when I heard that,” Mark stated, “because I thought, How many suicides has this fucking jackass actually seen?”.

So who does Mark think killed his brother?

According to recent reports, “It’s like in a Mob hit,” he said. “You try to find who the hit man was, and then you try to find who ordered the hit.” The hit man, he figured, could only be someone among a limited number of people: prison employees and other prisoners who had been on Jeffrey’s security tier. “Then the question becomes,” said Mark, “who would have the ability to orchestrate this in a federal prison, and who would have the ability to have the DOJ cover it up?” He couldn’t think of anyone besides Trump. (Trump has not been accused of any wrongdoing in connection to Jeffrey’s death; in a 2023 interview with Tucker Carlson, when asked whether Jeffrey could have been killed, he said, “Oh sure, it’s possible. I mean, I don’t really believe—I think he probably committed suicide.”).

I thought Mark and I had developed some rapport over the conversation, particularly after I mentioned that I’d attended the same Coney Island middle school where he and his brother had been students; I emphasized that I was trying to listen to him carefully and take him seriously. But there was a bit more rancor in his tone after I mentioned it was still difficult to believe that the Department of Justice could have successfully covered up the murder of the most high-profile prisoner in the world.

“If you don’t think that after what I just told you,” Mark said, “then you, sir, are a fucking idiot also.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'Fresh Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

In a recent development, here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, Upcoming Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox customers in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Newly introduced Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Industry observers note that amusingly, Latest Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Recent findings suggest that some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some GTA 6 hopefuls weren't chuffed when hearing the open-world crime fest is targeting 30fps on all consoles, but there's actually a way to circumvent that framerate cap thanks to a newly-discovered glitch on Xbox.

Before the game's meteoric launch, Rockstar Games confirmed that its crime fest was locked at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S - the studio acknowledged that even the PS5 Pro wasn't capable enough to simulate the game's massive, complicated world at higher framerates, either.

But Redditor Mewwie64's has found a way to run the game with an unlocked framerate by using a Quick Resume glitch on Xbox Series X - that's the handy feature that lets you switch between games from where you last left off, without needing to boot up each one from scratch.

Sources indicate that to run GTA 6 at 60fps or higher, you'll apparently need a 120hz display, an Xbox Series X, and the game itself on version 01.002.001. "This glitch may still work on later versions," the Redditor claims, "not sure.".

Industry observers note that the dedicated player also gave interested folks a tutorial on how to up those framerate caps: "Put your Xbox display settings to 60hz. Start GTA 6. Wait until you see the six stars in the intro. Change your display settings back to 120hz. Cold boot another game on your console via the Xbox Guide (The Xbox button) and without quitting GTA 6. Switch back to GTA 6." And, voila.

The Redditor does have one pretty big disclaimer, before you get too excited. "The game speed seems to be tied to your framerate," they write, so increasing the framerate might lead to certain animations looking faster than normal.

"It seems like the animations are at 2x speed or more in Jason's house in Chapter 1. I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more. But when you exit the house everything runs at an increased speed (The game world is likely tied to your framerate) but cutscenes work 100% fine without issues on higher framerates. Only the gameplay is sped up." Be warned, then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It notes the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, remarked to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

In a recent development, "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" announced by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Sources indicate that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

The Traitors: Newly introduced Blood returns for a second season in 2027. I am excited because I gladly welcome any Traitors. However, New Blood may be my least favorite of the franchise.

Industry observers note that it’s not necessarily a bad show, but it doesn’t seem to understand how to present itself in a more appealing package. As a Traitors superfan, that's made it extra frustrating to watch. Nonetheless, all hope isn’t lost, and I have some suggestions.

In a recent development, warning: The Traitors: New Blood spoilers are ahead. Proceed with caution.

For a long time, people used cliffhangers to entice readers or viewers to continuously return. It’s been part of the reality TV landscape for many decades. However, it’s not the only way to ensure viewership. The original The Traitors uses cliffhangers quite often, but it never felt as tedious as it does on The Traitors: New Blood.

Industry observers note that this could be because many of the other versions aren’t using a one-episode-a-week format. They either drop multiple episodes weekly or many on one day. Usually, Peacock’s version, for at least a few weeks, releases more than one episode weekly.. The Traitors: New Blood starts this way, but eventually shifts to one episode a week.

The switch is ultimately when the cliffhangers start to feel excessive. The episodes feel like a lot of nothing happens just to rush a cliffhanger ending. The end doesn’t have to be stuffed with cliffhangers. New Blood either needs longer episodes to flesh out the story better, or multiple episodes per week.

Industry observers note that A major appeal of The Traitors US is that it’s full of familiar faces. We know these reality TV stars, so we can get excited to see what they bring to the show. The Traitors: Latest Blood has some familiar influencers, but they are not as recognizable as reality TV stars and celebrities. Therefore, we want to get to know them.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that upcoming Blood didn’t showcase these players well. Victor and the Traitors stood out the most, but I wanted to get to know everyone a little bit. I wanted more rooting interest and people I want to see again on other reality TV shows. Season 2 needs a better balance of highlighting various personalities.

Fruitgate starts very interestingly and produced one of the season’s best episodes. However, the constant talk about it made me grow sour about the topic. It made me question if it’s fair that the Traitors have to make so many risky moves.

Sources indicate that the murders in plain sight have never bothered me before. They’re fun. However, New Blood’s version felt like it set the Traitors up for failure. I don’t want to lose that element of the show, but maybe it’s time to revamp it because having someone hand someone a fruit out of the blue feels too obvious.

Recent findings suggest that the Traitors: Canada Season 4 has a subtle version of this. The Traitors just have to bring a bowl of strawberries to breakfast. They don’t have to do anything but slightly encourage a few people to eat them.

I still have faith in The Traitors: Newly introduced Blood; I just think the producers need to reevaluate the show and not misunderstand why it isn’t working for many dedicated fans.

Tech Report: The designer of Atari's notorious E.T. likens the deluge of AI games to events that preceded the '80s industry crash: 'There was a glut of crap on the market'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the emergence of generative AI coding tools has numerous effects on the games industry this year, but the prominent of these is that it's made Steam an absolute nightmare to navigate.
  • According to recent reports, for many of us, this seems like a latest problem.
  • has been cited as a contributing factor in the US video game industry crash of 1983—one of many poor-quality 8-bit titles that hollowed out the gaming market in the States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the emergence of generative AI coding tools has numerous effects on the games industry this year, but the prominent of these is that it's made Steam an absolute nightmare to navigate. Since the summer, Steam (and other storefronts like itch.io) have been inundated with clones and AI slop games, as AI users turn to tools like Claude to output thousands of low-quality titles.

According to recent reports, for many of us, this seems like a latest problem. But for one veteran game developer, the scenario is all too familiar. Howard Scott Warshaw is the developer of numerous Atari 2600 games including Yars' Revenge and Raiders of the Lost Ark. But perhaps his most famous (or infamous) game is 1982's E.T. the Extra Terrestrial, the notorious tie-in game that was so terrible Atari buried unsold copies of it in the desert.

E.T. has been cited as a contributing factor in the US video game industry crash of 1983—one of many poor-quality 8-bit titles that hollowed out the gaming market in the States. It's here where Warshaw sees a parallel to today's emerging scenario, though he doesn't necessarily believe it will end in the same way.

Industry observers note that in a talk he gave at the DevGAMM Lisbon conference last week (via GamesIndustry.biz) Warshaw remarked upon how AI coding tools have seemed to rapidly sped up iteration times on game development. "People who used to spend weeks, months or years programming something can now do it in days with AI support," he explained.

"So what does this mean in game development? What it means is we're going to see a lot more games produced. You ever hear of the crash of '83 or '84, the big video game crash? They said the problem that happened in the crash, and I think that was true, was there was a glut of crap on the market, because the machine opened up and anybody could just pop a game out, and they did.".

Warshaw pointed out that, at the time "good games were still being made" but these games were "way overshadowed by the crap: and that created a real problem in the game industry." He sees a similar situation emerging now thanks to generative AI tools. "AI is going to have the same impact on a larger scale, because on one level, so many more people can now realise and create a video game than ever could before just using AI. And that's okay, but there's going to be a lot of crap, because most games suck. That's just the way it is.".

The reason for this, Warshaw says, is that, like all artistic endeavours "there's some things in life that everybody can see themselves doing, and the truth is most people who do it can't do it very well. And what AI is going to do is make that more possible for people who can't do it to do it." Yet while he thinks that most of the games that result from these ideas "aren't going to be very interesting" he also believes that "it's also going to enable the people who really do have some innovative, interesting and solid ideas to realise those, too.".

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

In short, Warshaw believes that AI will provoke a shift away from technology development to a greater focus on game design, which he ultimately believes is "actually going to be a super positive thing for the video game industry." He also said that, despite observing similar warning signs as in 1983, he doesn't "see the prospect of a crash in the video game industry" and instead expects to see a "reorganisation, where we need better filters to figure out a way to get rid of the garbage games".

Recent findings suggest that warshaw is certainly correct about AI tools resulting in a flood of crap, but I also think he himself overvalues the inherent worth of ideas in terms of what makes a great game. While ideas themselves can be inherently good or bad, no idea emerges from the creative process unscathed. Indeed, a major factor in creating art of any kind is engaging and grappling with that process, learning how to deal with the friction between the image in your head and what ends up on the page, or the canvas, or your scripting program. That mastery only comes through practice and experience. It cannot be outsourced or circumvented.

It has been revealed that but that doesn't change the fact that storefronts are at the moment being overwhelmed with terrible, AI-assisted games, and it's having all manner of knock-on effects. Earlier this month, Valve admitted it is "running behind" on approving Steam games because it has to keep re-reviewing them, and although Valve didn't cite AI as the cause of this, it's an awful coincidence that this has started happening as AI coding tools result in game submissions shooting through the roof.

Industry observers note that “That is the highest compliment you could give anyone!” Lux Pascal indicates after I tell her she looks like Jessica Paré’s Megan Draper from Mad Men. We’re at Chanel’s Watches and Fine Jewelry holiday dinner, held at Daniel Humm’s upcoming eponymous restaurant, Humm, in the West Village. Pascal is in a ’60s black modish leather minidress that she’s paired with a cat eye. On her wrists are Chanel’s Première Galon watch and Coco Crush bracelets, which, like her rings and earrings, are all dotted with diamonds. As I look around, most of the celebrities dressed by the brand are wearing looks that show off their French fine accessories. Ella Rubin, the Gen Z star of the hit teen TV show Sterling Point, has upgraded a simple pair of vintage Levi’s with a sleek black-and-gold Première Ribbon watch and several diamond rings. This is not a night for hidden gems.

According to recent reports, the Pierre Yovanovitch–designed restaurant is a verified Newly introduced York power room at the moment: There’s Derek Blasberg talking to Sarah Pidgeon about books—War and Peace gets a name-check—and Architectural Digest’s Amy Astley in a corner with Metropolitan Museum of Art board member Robert Denning. Indrė Rockefeller is here, as is stylist Vanessa Traina. In a feat of fun seating arrangements, the Chanel team has sat Rubin next to another young Ella: Beatty, the recent star of Monster and daughter of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening. (Although, with all due respect to those lovely Ellas, the two neighbors I’d most like to eavesdrop on are Devon Lee Carlson and Jack Harlow.) At the bar I hear two fashion people gossiping about industry hiring rumors: “Lauren Sherman indicates there’s two people in the running,” they whisper about some gig. I think I know what they’re talking about, but not enough to print it.

Laura Love and Devon Lee Carlson on November 17, 2026, in Fresh York City (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/WireImage).

According to recent reports, guests mill about because there’s much to mill about: Humm’s filled his restaurant with dozens of notable, site-specific artworks. Louise Bourgeois supplied 24 watercolor paintings, as well as a fantastical sterling silver cast of one of her sculptures, situated by the bar. (Tonight it’s serving mezcal sours with guava and an apple brandy highball.) Francesco Clemente painted not one, not two, but four celestial murals across two months, with motifs of abstract stars, animals, trains, and clocks. On the walls in the main dining room are 12 pigment drawings by Roni Horn. Then there’s all the work by Rashid Johnson: In the lounge—which for this event doubles as a red carpet—hangs his painting Untitled Homes. With Yovanovitch, he also built a custom host stand cast in aluminum and painted red. It’s so textural that you can see the fingerprints, and a number of guests gather around it as the maître d’ explains Johnson’s artistic process like he’s a docent at The Met.

Chanel has decorated the tables with long taper candles and arrangements of deep fuchsia peonies and burgundy garden roses. Waiters serve Humm’s signature everything caviar bagels. When I think about ordering something other than the chicken, a waiter tells me not to. He’s right.

Singer-songwriter girlsweetvoiced.

Sources indicate that at the end of the night, after most guests are a few glasses of red wine (or martinis) deep, Pidgeon herself grabs a microphone. The event, as it turns out, has a surprise performer: girlsweetvoiced. “She captures something that’s very honest,” Pidgeon notes of the emerging singer-songwriter, who then belts out a cover of Joni Mitchell’s “California.” Title aside, it’s been a very New York night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

Sources indicate that and that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game released in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

According to recent reports, leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Upcoming Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Recent findings suggest that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that no matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list, you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. So naturally you must be wondering if you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, or whether you need to pack everything in before hitting a point of no return.

I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.

According to recent reports, you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status, your criminal profile, whether you paid into family savings, and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index.

Recent findings suggest that this means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a new save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch.

Sources indicate that from this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again.

According to recent reports, the GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. Industry observers note that we've seen Glen Powell chase tornadoes, fly airplanes and play a football player in disguise. Next, he'll be transforming into a country singer for The Comeback King, a comedy he's collaborating with Judd Apatow on that will premiere on the 2027 movie schedule in February. So, what inspired him to put the cowboy hat back on and sing? Well, it turns out Twisters and shotgunning a beer with Luke Combs had something to do with it.

It has been revealed that it’s not surprising to hear the Texas native is tapping into his country roots with The Comeback King, but I was surprised to find out the story would follow Powell as Aubrey King, a disgraced famous country singer who must revive his career, and that it was a comedy. After rave reviews for Season 2 of Powell’s Hulu comedy Chad Powers, I’m glad to see him stepping further into the comedic landscape after a string of action films like Top Gun: Maverick, Twisters, and The Running Man. However, I did not expect him to tell Katie and Tech giant that the inspiration behind this upcoming project stemmed from drinking beer with Luke Combs:.

According to recent reports, I think it was when we were putting together Twisters. We were putting together the Twisters soundtrack that had, you know, Ella [Langley] and Megan Moroney, Bailey Zimmerman, Luke [Combs]. You know, it was like we had a great community, and I was like ‘Man, I just wanna be a part of this world.’ Probably right after I shotgunned beers with Luke Combs on stage. I was like, ‘I need to live here. I wanna do beers for breakfast just like Luke.’.

Recent findings suggest that I can’t say I blame the Hit Man actor for getting caught up in that moment with his fellow Twisters castmates and Luke Combs. Together, they all shotgunned beer on stage at Combs’ NYC concert back in the summer of 2024, and the video went viral on TikTok.

As Powell mentions, he got a taste of the country music life putting together the Twisters movie soundtrack, which hit no. 3 on the Billboard country album charts that summer, with Luke Combs’ “Ain’t No Love In Oklahoma” spending 15 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100.

Recent findings suggest that A tale as old as Rocky, if you want a part in a specific film, write it yourself. According to Rolling Stone, Producer Kevin Misher connected Powell with Apatow shortly after the idea for The Comeback King was born, and the Scream Queens actor and the mind behind Knocked Up wrote the script together. This will be Apatow’s first directorial feature film since The Bubble (2022) and The King of Staten Island (2020).

I’m already sold on The Comeback King from the trailer alone. It’s got hilarious roasts, a redemption arc, and a ton of heart, all the hallmarks of a great Judd Apatow film. In The Comeback King, we see Glen Powell live out his wildest “beer for breakfast” fantasies (a nod to Luke Combs “Don’t Tempt Me”), until it all comes crashing down after his pop star girlfriend (Madelyn Cline) cheats and ruins his reputation. King then returns to his old college where his career all started, for redemption and maybe a upcoming shot at love. Check out the trailer below, and see if you can name the insane number of country music cameos:.

It has been revealed that how Glen Powell was able to once again assemble the Avengers of country music, I’ll never know. But I’m super excited to see the likes of Miranda Lambert, Jelly Roll, Brad Paisley, and Shaboozey bring their A-game alongside Powell in this epic ensemble comedy when it premieres on February 5, 2027. While we wait for that, I think we should all say thank you to Luke Combs too for helping inspire this film that looks like it'll be a lot of country fun.

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

It has been revealed that "Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

In a recent development, another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among fresh and returning players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood.

I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN, Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom.

In a recent development, "A massive part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer.".

Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this substantial machine is always running even when players aren't there.".

Sources indicate that while this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day, either.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Recent findings suggest that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • Sources indicate that "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Recent findings suggest that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

Sources indicate that "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek claims the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

Sources indicate that cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nintendo apparently agonized over The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's emotional ending cutscene.
  • Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi - the developer who also served as game director on Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom - said as much in an interview with Game Informer, explaining that he's "very, very happy" to hear that the remake's finale is having an emotional affect on some players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo apparently agonized over The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's emotional ending cutscene.

Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi - the developer who also served as game director on Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom - said as much in an interview with Game Informer, explaining that he's "very, very happy" to hear that the remake's finale is having an emotional affect on some players.

"That cutscene – cutscenes in general – but that cutscene specifically is something that we, as a dev team, heavily discussed," Fujibayashi says of the game's ending. "Because of the limitations of the technology back in the day, there might have been things that we weren't able to convey fully, whether it's because of the tempo of the game… whatever it is.".

It has been revealed that almost three decades of hardware improvements and technical know-how let Nintendo realize the scene fully, as it was first intended all those years ago on the N64. "And so, when we approached this remake, we wanted to make sure that we captured that moment in the way that we wanted to express it. So that the right kinds of emotions are evoked, and that we can convey the emotion and the story that we wanted to at that moment," Fujibayashi adds.

The Zelda maestro is just "really relieved to hear" people are having strong reactions to the end of the game and its full-circle send off.

The Switch 2's Ocarina of Time seems to have been welcomed with glowing reactions across the board. Nier Automata's Yoko Taro just had to pick it up, Final Fantasy Resonance lead said it was a masterclass in remakes, and the game also managed to become the best-selling US physical release of the year after just one week.

The last time CinemaBlend caught up with the showrunners, they told us they’re trying to “slow burn” the relationship between Percy and Annabeth. When I caught up with them again, Jonathan E. Steinberg delved into where we’re at this season with their dynamic, saying this:.

And, I think that puts a lot of pressure on the moments in which they are to be making those moments meaningful. And, I think it puts a lot of pressure on what it puts them through to be separated from each other and what they would do to make sure the other's OK, and how much you feel that.

It has been revealed that oh, I feel it. I mean, what sticks out to me so far is that dance scene between them in Episode 1. After Percy famously told Annabeth he would “burn it all down” for her last season if he had to, you can feel this unsaid chemistry between them. However, in true teenage boy fashion, Percy shoots down the comment when Annabeth brings it up. Then, right before she gets captured by the manticore, Percy looks like he was about to risk everything to try to save her if Artemis didn’t pull him off the ledge.

And, as someone who's seen the next two episodes (but I promise I won’t tell), there’s even more where that came from. Steinberg also mentioned this during our recent chat:.

Industry observers note that so, I think it does its job as the middle chapter of the book series and kind of where we are in the bigger story. I think by the time you get to the end of the season, you feel it. If you are somebody who read these books and knows where this is going and knows where it ends, the show is not just tracking that, but it's adding really meaningful depth to what that moment will mean eventually, and to what they mean to each other in the moment now.

Sources indicate that season 3 really feels like the sweet spot for Percy and the rest of the cast, where they are at the right age for the show to mature a bit more, and that makes me more excited for what’s to come. I know there’s always discourse around the book changes in TV shows like this, but I like what’s been done so far. For one, we’re getting to see Annabeth’s time in captivity, and we’re also getting more Percabeth moments ahead of the pair going from friends to romantic partners.

Sources indicate that there’s so much more to get excited for regarding the adaptation of The Titan’s Curse! Two new episodes will drop on Disney+ and Hulu every Friday until finale week on December 11.

Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond—Revisit 007’s Style Legacy Here

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There must be no male character across film history who has done more for menswear—and for the suit—than Bond, James Bond.
  • Recent findings suggest that that is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes.
  • Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There must be no male character across film history who has done more for menswear—and for the suit—than Bond, James Bond.

Recent findings suggest that that is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes. And yet, as Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, Sean Connery, and other dangerously handsome men have proven, a mere suit does not a 007 make. This is why, despite Bond being one of the most popular film characters of all time, you will rarely see ordinary men dare to take him on as a Halloween costume. There’s simply more to making Bond than a good tux.

Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953. In the announcement clip for Pattinson’s casting, the actor looks the part in a black tuxedo and white shirt, but it’s his eyes, which pierce through the camera rather than down the barrel of his gun, that do most of the talking and offer a suggestion of what Pattinson’s Bond may have to offer. Will he be a little darker and tortured, like his take on Batman? Or perhaps his Bond will be louche and somewhat pricklier.

In a recent development, A safer bet to make is that he will look good. One of the most enduring legacies of the James Bond franchise is how stylish both the character of Bond and the universe built around him have always been. Bond has appeared classic and timeless in style during each of the franchise’s eras, but hindsight offers a much richer perspective.

Pierce Brosnan, The World Is Not Enough, 1999.

Daniel Craig, Casino Royale, 2006.

As portrayed through the decades in the property’s famous title sequence, Bond is a silhouette—a classic, timeless silhouette. Fleming established the look in his development of the character when he made the suit his primary uniform. But it is Terence Young, the director of the first 007 films, who is responsible for the visual definition of Bond.

When Connery was cast as Bond for the first film, Dr. No (1962), Young, an avid wearer of suits himself, took him to his own tailor, Anthony Sinclair. We can credit Sinclair with developing the original silver screen Bond look: The suit was lighter in fit and tailoring than most other English suits at the time. The Bond suit had a soft shoulder and waist, but a strong, wide chest and a low button stance that elongated its wearer. Every Bond suit that’s followed has been measured to the standard of Sinclair’s work, and every Bond actor has had to compete with Connery’s charisma while wearing it.

Roger Moore, The Spy Who Loved Me, 1977.

According to recent reports, brosnan and his Brioni suits were indicative of the 1990s corporate look of the time. Craig wore Brioni too, but only for Casino Royale; Tom Ford created his subsequent suiting, which often stood out for the slim fit popular in the 2010s. Most memorable sartorially is Roger Moore’s take through the ’70s and ’80s, which often deviated from the sleekness that had come to define Bond by creating a little frisson with lighter, brighter fabrics and a bolder sense of playfulness.

The character of Bond, and the actor personifying him at a given time, have also become representative of a certain male standard: Connery in the ’60s, tan and athletic, or Brosnan in the ’90s, polished with lithe elegance. And then came Craig, whose casting was met with skepticism, to put it lightly. His arrival was marked by the image of the actor walking out of the ocean in tight swim trunks in Casino Royale. His strong legs, rounded shoulders, and sculpted, hairless chest cemented then and there the idea of what a leading man had become and would look like for the next two decades.

Daniel Craig as James Bond, Casino Royale, 2006.

Also synonymous with Bond are his watch and many vehicles. Most recently, Bond cars have all been made by Aston Martin, though Brosnan drove some spectacular BMWs. The official Bond timepiece since Brosnan’s turn has been Omega. But before such kinds of commercial partnerships were commonplace in Hollywood, Connery wore watches by Rolex, Gruen, and Breitling, while Moore wore pieces by Seiko.

With the news that Pattinson is taking on the mantle, an equally pressing question emerges: Who will be the first fresh Bond girl?

Some of the most memorable moments in the franchise’s history have been anchored by women. Halle Berry’s emergence from the ocean in an orange bikini and a white belt safekeeping a knife was only made better by the fact that this moment was an homage to the first Bond girl, Ursula Andress, and her ivory two-piece featuring a belt for her own weapon. Then there was Eva Green as Vesper Lynd in a slinky Versace dress in Casino Royale. But it didn’t get better than Grace Jones in A View to a Kill. As May Day, a fabulous femme fatale, Jones wore costumes designed for her by Azzedine Alaïa. How could anyone measure up?

Halle Berry and Pierce Brosnan, Die Another Day, 2002.

Roger Moore and Grace Jones, 1985, A View To a Kill, 1985.

Recent findings suggest that of course, we will have to see how stylistic choices play out in the 26th Bond film, which, like Bond movies of the past, will become emblematic of the era in which we live. It will also, as a creative project, have to contend with the way Hollywood operates today. The fact that Amazon now has full creative control over the franchise—the company acquired MGM, a co-owner of the Bond franchise rights, for $8.45 billion in 2022 and later struck a deal with the other co-owners in regard to creative authority—is the primary indication of that.

Recent findings suggest that pattinson will also be the first Bond with airtight fashion-brand deals. Craig was an Omega ambassador as an extension of his role as Bond, which made him a household name, and the 007s who came before him operated within a film industry that was not as closely connected to fashion.

Sources indicate that also unlike his predecessors, Pattinson is stepping into the role as a bona fide movie star who has appeared in three other major franchises (Harry Potter, Twilight, and Batman). He’s already one of the most prolific and bankable stars of his generation, and an undeniable part of being a movie star today is becoming the face of a franchise, a brand, or a product.

Recent findings suggest that in September, Pattinson was announced as a global ambassador for Jaeger-LeCoultre, a Swiss watchmaker. But 007 has worn Omega watches onscreen for decades, a partnership between the brand and the franchise that dates back to the Brosnan years. If Omega’s partnership with the franchise remains for this newly introduced installment, it could present a potential conflict if Pattinson’s contract with Jaeger stipulates that he is not allowed to wear another brand’s watch onscreen or front related campaigns for competitors. It may sound like a banal preoccupation, as Pattinson has only just been cast, but there are millions of dollars at play, and actors today often make as much money from brand deals as they do from their turns onscreen.

Pattinson has also been an ambassador for Dior since 2013, serving first as a fragrance ambassador and subsequently as a face for ready-to-wear Dior Homme; he was originally tapped under Kris Van Assche, with his ambassadorship extending through Kim Jones’s tenure at the renamed Dior Men and now continuing with Jonathan Anderson at the helm of the French mega-brand. Will Anderson be providing his suits? The Irish designer has costumed films before, working with Luca Guadagnino on Challengers, Queer, and the upcoming Artificial. To design for the major screen would hardly be a stretch for him.

In a recent development, the real question is more existential: Should Bond wear high fashion? To return to the idea of the 007 silhouette, that in itself is counterintuitive to Pattinson saving the world in one of Anderson’s menswear takes on the famous Dior Bar jacket, with its nipped waist and slightly flared hem. And yet in this brave latest world of brand deals, anything is possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet mentioned mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet mentioned mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which rolled out last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the organization is run, with the publisher saying its fresh operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

It has been revealed that outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft states the newly introduced structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active people over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

Industry observers note that the news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft revealed in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

In a recent development, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a newly introduced Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

It has been revealed that upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Sources indicate that samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

Industry observers note that for anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

Industry observers note that the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

Moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

According to recent reports, for a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

Sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

For smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose claims improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

According to recent reports, samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

For something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That stated, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

If you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

The LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's right now $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

At just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That said, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Sources indicate that black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

GTA 6 Riata locations: How to restore the second car for Wyman

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You'll have to track down the GTA 6 Riata locations to fix the second Classic Car Collection vehicle for Wyman.
  • There are three Riatas you need to scan with the WAiNK It app to fix up this classic off-roading 4x4, one in Key Lento itself, one near the naval base at Goose Key, and a final one in Shoeless Keys.
  • This is the first one Wyman asks you to find, near the PD in the Keys.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'll have to track down the GTA 6 Riata locations to fix the second Classic Car Collection vehicle for Wyman. He'll text you a little while after you complete the Transgressor, this time sending you to the Key Lento area, unfortunately a rather long drive when you're likely still at the motel near Port Gellhorn.

There are three Riatas you need to scan with the WAiNK It app to fix up this classic off-roading 4x4, one in Key Lento itself, one near the naval base at Goose Key, and a final one in Shoeless Keys.

This is the first one Wyman asks you to find, near the PD in the Keys. It's under a brown stilt house north of Leonida Key Lento Mini-mart and the Shrimp 'n Save, on that northernmost road running through the Key. Find the brown stilt house, as in the video above, then just head underneath to scan the car.

This second one is located in Southwind, on Goose Key, the island with the Mile Zero Air Station to the west of Key Lento—you will have visited here for a mission early in the game. The junked car is under another brown stilt house at the end of the road down to the east from the Xero Gas - Southwind station, on the right just before the sea.

This third one is located behind the ruined gas station just to the north of Grassrivers Cafe & Deli in Shoeless Keys. The tricky part is that this is a four-star area (because of the final missions in Chapter 1), so you'll want to be quick as otherwise a police chopper will come and spot you. When you turn off the main road, the garage is on your left before you reach the cafe itself, with the car just behind.

Somehow, I forgot to record this one, but I still show the location in the clip above behind the gas station (just without the car since it was gone when I re-recorded).

Once you have all three, Wyman will tell you to wait a little while, and then will call and ask you to Buck him $1,500 for the labour. Select the payment request in the text, or do it manually in the app. A little while after the money is sent, you'll get a map marker for Wyman's scrapyard, where you can pick up this completed classic car.

Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • In a recent development, this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • It has been revealed that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

In a recent development, this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

It has been revealed that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

According to recent reports, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.
